sections.title: Sound of A
paragraphs: You call this letter (A) /eɪ/. Its main sound is the vowel in (apple) /æ.pəl/, which means an apple. This letter has four different sounds.

sections.title: Pronouncing A
paragraphs: For the first sound, drop your jaw low, widen your lips, and push your tongue forward. Next, glide from a middle vowel upward, moving your tongue toward the roof of your mouth. Then, relax your entire mouth completely to make a quick, weak vowel. Finally, open your mouth wide and keep your tongue low and flat. Feel your throat vibrate with your fingers for all four sounds.

sections.title: Spelling of A
paragraphs: In a closed syllable with stress, you say the sound /æ/ as in (cat) /kæt/. In an open syllable or before a consonant with silent e, say the sound /eɪ/ as in (make) /meɪk/. In an unstressed syllable, use the weak sound /ə/ as in (sofa) /soʊ.fə/. Before certain consonants like r or lm, say the deep sound /ɑː/ as in (father) /fɑː.ðər/.

sections.title: Common Mistakes
paragraphs: Do not replace the wide sound /æ/ with a simple vowel like the one in (calm) /kɑːm/. Drop your jaw lower and spread your lips wider. Do not stress the weak sound /ə/ at the end of a word. Keep that final sound very short and relaxed.
